Test Scenario: Verify getter and setter statement coverage
Test Data:
Product ID: WMS-101
Name: MacBook Pro
Test Steps:
1. Instantiate Product
2. Set field values
3. Call getters
Expected Result: Getter methods should return assigned values.

Test Scenario: Verify toJson() branch with null description
Expected Result: JSON should contain null description without crash.

Test Scenario: Verify toJson() branch with valid description
Expected Result: Description should be quoted in JSON output.
Should return empty string immediately.
Quotes should be escaped properly.
Backslash should be escaped properly.

Test Scenario: Verify price decimal formatting in toJson()
Expected Result: Price should format with 2 decimals.
Content-Type header should be application/json.
JSON should contain success:false and message.
Complete request body should be read.
Should return empty string safely.
Map should contain parsed key-value pairs.
Connection should use environment variable URL.
Configuration should load from db.properties.
RuntimeException should be thrown.
Cached configuration should be reused.
PreparedStatement parameters 1-6 should bind safely.
Duplicate key error 1062 should be caught.
Should return empty List with size 0.
Loop should map all 7 rows to Product objects.

Test Scenario: Verify getProductById() branch when record exists
Expected Result: Populated Product object should be returned.

Test Scenario: Verify getProductById() branch when not found
Expected Result: Null should be returned safely.
Affected row count > 0 should be returned.
Should return null for non-existent product.
InnoDB row lock should be placed.
Transaction should commit atomically.

Test Scenario: Verify reduceStock() decision on excess quantity
Expected Result: Rollback should occur and exception thrown.

Test Scenario: Verify reduceStock() rollback in catch block
Expected Result: Catch block should call conn.rollback().
Quantity should decrement and commit.

Test Scenario: Verify resource cleanup in finally block
Expected Result: All JDBC resources must be closed safely.
